Step 2

Look up the terms

+
+

A status is always a word, a glyph and a colour. Colour is never the only signal.

+
+
Pass

What was counted or checked passed. A count says what it was counted from.

+
Fail

A recorded check or verdict failed. It keeps its own rung and is never folded into a count.

+
Warn

A gap or disagreement in the trail. Read the sentence beside it before relying on the value.

+
Pending

Not done yet, so there is nothing to check yet.

+
Not built

Not built yet. There is no red, green, refactor, QA step or sign-off to show, and the page says so instead of inventing one.

+
+

Terms used on the other screens.

  • Rung. One numbered step in a story. The number is the step's position in the order, not a time.
  • Red, green, refactor. The values of a commit's TDD trailer. A rule page puts the red commit above the green one, so you read the order from position.
  • Attempt. One pass of a node through the build loop. Every attempt keeps its own rung; retries are never folded into a counter.
  • gate.stub. A recorded check, shown with what it expected and what it returned.
  • Verdict. A reviewer's or security agent's PASS or FAIL, recorded verbatim.
  • Finding. A problem a verdict raised. A later commit's Fixes-Finding trailer names the one it fixes.
  • Human decision. A point where David approved, steered or merged. They are listed together on the Human decisions screen.
  • Git-only. A node with no trail files; what is shown comes from git alone.
  • Snapshot. The commit this site was compiled from, stamped in step 5.

+# inv-008: W3's attempt-2 review FAIL comes from red-step gaps, not the A1 route
+## Question
+Does the reviewer's attempt-2 FAIL of ui/W3 (P1 R1, R2, R3) come from gaps the red step left and from the request log's data model, rather than from a defect a previous route introduced?
+## Hypothesis
+R1 and R2 are red-step gaps: t1 scoped renew-inside-the-window out of the e2e because the live API has no demo clock and nothing covered it at the screen, and R2's 'Card' equals the renew screen's fallback by accident. R3 comes from the `LoggedExchange` type the red tester stubbed without headers and with parsed bodies, which the builder followed, while the wb-requests reference draws both header sets. Disproved if the reference draws no headers or raw bodies, if a test already reaches the renew success state at the screen, or if the A1 route (fd987b6, d16f39e, ab061ce, e795f19) introduced any of R1–R3.
+## Evidence
+- docs/trace/ui/W3/verdicts/A2-reviewer.json: FAIL, P1 R1–R3, P2 R4–R6
+- docs/trace/ui/W3/verdicts/A2-security.json: PASS, no findings
+- docs/trace/ui/W3/findings/A2.md: the investigator's diagnosis of every reviewer finding (I1–I6)
+- docs/trace/ui/W3/findings/A1.md: the attempt-1 gate route, for line positions and scope
+- docs/trace/ui/W3/packet/: diff.patch, trailers.txt, gates.jsonl at e674cdc
+- docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-requests/populated.html: draws request and response headers inside http-exchange
+- docs/ui/derived/W3/wb-renew/screen.json: success terms come from a labelled fake-clock source, not a live run
+## Findings
+**Yes.** All three P1s date from the red step (8c26d5d, ac94134, 75f3244). The two P2s in screen code date from the green step (50d3d4e). The A1 route introduced none of them, and none repeats an A1 fingerprint. A1 was a gate route over the 8 failing tests, and a missing test never fails a gate. With t2 stub and t3 Pause 1 skipped under the lean loop, nothing ran the behaviour tests against canned screens or put them beside the references before review. See [findings/A2.md](../../trace/ui/W3/findings/A2.md).
+- I1 (R1, new, tests): no test drives wb-renew to an accepted renewal. The e2e scopes it out (`tests/web/e2e/W3/wb-5.spec.ts:3-5`), and the only success test is a client unit test on a hand-built 201 (`tests/web/unit/client/wb-5.test.ts:78-89`). The screen's success branch (`RenewPolicy.tsx:84`, `:95-96`, `:201-206`) never runs under test. Tester alone.
+- I2 (R2, new, tests): the default-method test sells with 'Card' (`wb-5.spec.ts:88`, `:91`), which is also the first-paint value and the fallback (`RenewPolicy.tsx:24`, `:63`). Tester alone.
+- I3 (R3, new, client model): `LoggedExchange` has no headers and keeps parsed bodies (`src/web/app/data/api.ts:368-374`, `:393-418`), and the red unit test pins that shape with `toEqual` on five keys (`tests/web/unit/client/wb-7.test.ts:20-22`, `:41`). The kit's HttpExchange already takes headers and exact text. Tester (strengthen the red assertions, add a header e2e), then builder.
+- I4 (R4, P2, U7): the Card fallback at `RenewPolicy.tsx:24`, `:63`, which is I2's code side.
+- I5 (R5, P2, U7): a pending request is shown as status 0 (`RequestLogPage.tsx:26`), because the kit's request-log row has no pending state.
+- I6 (R6, P2, U7): references are built from `Date.now()` (`wb-5.spec.ts:10`, `wb-7.spec.ts:11`). Untestable as app behaviour.
+## Recommendations
+```yaml recommendations
+- {kind: amend-node, target: ui/W3, reason: "Run the A2 route as tester then builder in one round: the tester adds the routed-201 renew success e2e (I1) and the DirectDebit default-method test (I2), each passing at HEAD and failing against a screen that ignores the data, and strengthens wb-7's red assertions to require headers and exact wire text plus a response-headers e2e (I3, recorded as a strengthening); the builder then carries headers and raw text through loggingFetch, the log page and the drawer to the kit unchanged", status: proposed}
+```
+## Why
+The attempt-3 stop on ui/W3: the reviewer's FAIL at attempt 2 (round A2) made `attempt` 3 (feature SKILL §5).
+## Approach
+Read-only. I read the parent's trail and dispatched the investigator once with the question, the hypothesis and the evidence paths. The 30-minute box held: the investigation started at 20:58:33Z and the findings were back at about 21:02Z.
+## Rejected alternatives
+- Fix R1–R3 by the tester alone. I3 cannot be closed in tests: the client drops the headers and the wire text before anything renders, so the builder must change `loggingFetch` and its two consumers.
+- Make R3 a kit gap. The kit's HttpExchange already accepts request and response headers and an exact-text body (`HttpExchange.tsx:17-19`, `:29-31`), so the gap is in the client's model, not the kit.

    I1FixedTestable

    Symptom
    live POST /policies/{ref}/claims returns 500 with an InvalidOperationException saying RecordClaimRequest has validation metadata on record property 'Description' that will be ignored.
    Cause
    CancellationContracts.cs:38-40 declares RecordClaimRequest as a positional record and targets its DataAnnotations at the generated properties ('[property: Required] DateOnly? ClaimDate' at :39 and '[property: MaxLength(500)] string? Description' at :40). MVC builds a positional record through its primary constructor, so it reads validation metadata from the constructor parameters. When it finds validators on a property that maps to a constructor parameter, it throws during object-model validation instead of quietly ignoring them. The throw happens on every request whose body deserialises into a RecordClaimRequest (PoliciesController.cs:63 binds it from the body), so the happy path, 404, 422 and DataAnnotations-400 cases all become 500s. The stub's canned body at :65 never runs. The exception names only 'Description', but ClaimDate at :39 has exactly the same pattern and is the same cause (not a separate finding). Fixing only :40 would probably just move the exception to ClaimDate; the code doesn't show why MVC reported Description first. COULD-2 says 'claimDate required, description optional, max 500', and the architecture contract says required DTO members are 'nullable and [Required]'. Both constraints have to be enforced as a 400, not dropped or turned into a 500.
